title: Halving and Bit-Length Accumulation
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $m$ be one of the four codec modes, and let $y$ be a bit string and $B$ a natural number. For any assignment $v$ of natural numbers to the $21$ registers, suppose every register value is at most $B$ and the value in register $r_{m Wp}$ plus the length of the binary expansion of the value in register $r_{m T}$ is at most $B$. Then the codec register program can reach its copy phase for $E$ from its halving-counter test state, changing register $r_{m T}$ to $0$ and register $r_{m Wp}$ to its former value plus that binary expansion length; throughout the run, its prescribed safety condition holds and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register value in $v$ is at most $B$
